findings.title: Equivalent rectangle rotations bypass deduplication
findings.body: Deduplication compares RotationAngle with a raw absolute difference. A rectangular footing has the same physical orientation at angles differing by π, but reversed CAD traversal can make Rectangle2 report those equivalent angles differently. Overlapping or duplicated CAD outlines can therefore survive both deduplication passes and cause multiple foundations to be placed at the same location. Compare angular distance modulo π, with appropriate handling for swapped dimensions or square footprints.

findings.title: Elevation rounding can split connected outlines
findings.body: Loose lines are grouped by independently rounding their average Z values into 0.01-foot buckets. This is not tolerance-based clustering: averages of 0.0049 and 0.0051 feet differ by only 0.0002 feet but fall into different groups. Lines belonging to one slightly noisy CAD rectangle can consequently be sent to separate extractor calls, leaving neither group closed and silently omitting the foundation.

findings.title: New placement behavior lacks reviewable focused tests
findings.body: Every included test exercises only CadParserService.ExtractFromSegments. None constructs FoundationPlacementOrchestrator or verifies adapter calls, invalid-value filtering, type-creation failure, or forwarding of coordinates and rotation. The comment referring to tests in a different review batch cannot provide evidence for this exact reviewed file list, so regressions in the newly added placement implementation would pass the included validation.

findings.title: End-to-end test does not validate CAD-derived rotation
findings.body: The only parser-to-placement test uses an axis-aligned rectangle and never asserts RotationAngle. It therefore passes if CAD extraction always returns zero rotation, even though foundations parsed from rotated CAD would be placed with the wrong orientation. Add a rotated rectangle case and assert the resulting placement angle, including any length/width normalization convention.
